messages:
Maria (eng-platform): Heads-up — BigBank asked for a one-off routing tweak: pin their traffic to a lower-latency pool for the next 3 days while they run a load test. Can we do this without creating a permanent exception?
Samir: we have the per-tenant pin APIs, but they create an audit entry + require change approval. do they need a UI flow or API only?
Maria (eng-platform): API-only is fine for them, but security wants a short-lived allow rule and an explicit deny fallback after expiry. auditability is non-negotiable. :lock:
Jia: short-lived rules are supported if we add an expires_at field to the routing override. currently we only store manual ttl in metadata (not enforced).
Alex: that sounds risky — if the enforcement path isn't in the router, TTLs will become paperwork. we should have the gateway drop overrides after expiry.
Samir: agreed. Implementation idea: add 'expires_at' to the override schema and check it in routing eval. lightweight check: if now > expires_at, skip override.
Maria (eng-platform): can we also scope by header? BigBank will send X-Tenant-ID header. want to ensure no accidental cross-tenant pinning.
Jia: yep, new policy shape proposal: { match: { header: { "X-Tenant-ID": "bigbank" } }, action: { route: "low-latency-pool", expires_at: "<iso>" }, audit: true }
Alex: throw in a denylist precedence rule — if tenant is on org-level denylist, overrides must not apply. precedence order: denylist > per-tenant override > default routing.
Samir: sounds good. will need console UX: a quick 'pin for N hours' button that emits that policy. Also surface the expiry in the audit log and route history.
Maria (eng-platform): ops wants a fallback plan: if pinned pool runs out of capacity, fall back to 'best-effort' with an alert to SRE. how to model that in policy?
Jia: action could be a list with ordered fallbacks: { action: [{ route: "low-latency-pool" }, { route: "best-effort", notify: "sre-team" }] } and runtime will try first then fallback.
Alex: runtime change footprint is moderate. main perf cost is adding expiry + header match to the hot path. we can micro-opt: compile header matcher to a bitmask for common headers.
Samir: security asked for a signed override token for API-created pins so we can validate origin. ops-bot can emit an event when override created.
ops-bot: override.created tenant=bigbank creator=support-bot ttl=72h id=ovr_9c1f2a audit_link=https://console/redwood/audit/ovr_9c1f2a
Maria (eng-platform): sample curl for the API we expect to expose (for docs):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/overrides 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{
    "match": { "header": { "X-Tenant-ID": "bigbank" } },
    "action": { "route": "low-latency-pool", "expires_at": "2026-03-25T18:00:00Z" },
    "created_by": "support-bot",
    "signed_token": "<jwt>"
  }'
```
Samir: thanks. follow-ups for implementation: (1) storage migration to index expires_at, (2) router eval change, (3) console pin button + confirmation with audit, (4) tests for precedence with denylist.
Jia: I'll draft the schema PR and a tiny compatibility shim for runtime. propose feature flag 'tenant-routing-ttl' for 2 weeks rollout.
Alex: add perf benchmark before/after. if header checks add >2% p95, we need to optimize.
Maria (eng-platform): ok team — please post PR links here when ready. I'll coordinate with support to schedule the pin window for BigBank. Thanks :raised_hands:
ops-bot: reminder scheduled for 2026-03-22T09:00:00Z (notify: #eng-oncall)
